title: DM ONLY - Mushrooms, Drugs, Alcohol Drinks
content:
Rule - Daterra's Survival Mushroom Foraging Rule

  • She rolls Survival. If environment is plentiful, Survival DC 1o. Normal places, DC12-14. Underdark is usually DC15, 20, or higher.

  • If she beat the DC, for every 1 over the DC she can get 1 bingo chip. For every 3 over the DC she can get a rolled Special Mushroom (from Feywild or Underdark Rolltables). She can mix and match.

  • When first taking the drug, make a Con save to resist addiction.
  • Then if drug isn't taken again within the Satiation period, make another Con save. If failed, user is still addicted, and must take Withdrawal Effects.
  • Every day after that that the user continues to not take the drug, user must try to make the Con save again. If failed, continue Withdrawal Effects and try again next day.
  • If an addict succeeds on a save, they continue to take Withdrawal Effects and must make it another whole day and succeed on a 2nd save at a +3 DC! Only after succeeding this 2nd save are they cured of addiction. If 2nd save is failed, they start over and need 2 successive successes.

OVERDOSE? If more than one dose is taken in a 24-hour period, the user could take effects like:

  • immediately falls unconscious for 1d4 hours (Fort DC 18 negates).

  • takes 2d6 points of damage.

  • side effects doubled.

  • make a separate save (Con DC 25) or die in terrible pain.

  • paralyzes the user for 2d4 hours.

  • nauseated for 1d4 × 10 minutes

  • numbing stupor for 2d4 hours. The user can only take partial actions until the stupor wears off.

  • Disad on all of an Ability until long rest.

  • user becomes catatonic (Fort DC 15 negates).



List of Mushrooms / Fungi


Violet Fungus

Creature / Hazard — harvestable fungus

  • Found In: Underdark, Material Plane (Surface) forests near treants. Also found in Shedaklah, the 222nd layer of the Abyss.

  • Value: Live specimen — nothing, it's a hazard. Harvested Tendril Extract — 25–45 gp per vial. Necrotic spore powder — 20–35 gp per pouch.

  • Appearance: 4–7 ft tall, deep purple to dull gray, sometimes violet with purple spots. Four long leafy tendrils droop motionlessly until something comes within reach. Root-like feelers allow slow movement. Nearly indistinguishable from an ordinary large mushroom while still.

  • Lore: Violet fungi sometimes grow on living treants, roots feeding on the treant for sustenance. In exchange they defend the treant from bark-eating parasites. An ancient treant draped in violet fungus is not diseased — it is armed.

  • Crafting — Violet Fungus Rot Salve: Tendril Extract + crushed bone + any oil or alcohol, Herbalist or Alchemist's Supplies and proficiency (1 hr during a Rest, no roll required) = a corrosive salve. Applied to rope, leather, or wood: dissolves completely in 10 minutes. Applied to flesh as a weapon: DC 14 Con save or 1d8 necrotic damage and wound cannot be healed by mundane means (no Hit Dice recovery) for 24 hours.

  • Crafting — Necrotic Weapon Coat: Fresh tendril secretion applied to a blade (Action or Bonus Action, DC 11 Survival, gloves required): next hit deals an extra 1d6 necrotic damage.

  • Addiction: None


Zygom Mushroom

Fungal Creature / Hazard

  • Found In: Underdark; Chult jungles (Material Plane Surface); Pazunia (1st layer of the Abyss); Shedaklah (222nd layer of the Abyss, domain of Zuggtmoy)

  • Value: Blue milk worth 30–60 gp per vial to alchemists and poisoners. A live colony is uncontainable — it will infest whoever carries it.

  • Appearance: A colony of small pale-capped mushrooms growing in a cluster. Faint blue sheen on the underside of the caps where the milk is stored. DC 15 Nature or Medicine to identify before touching.

  • Lore: Zygoms don't hunt — they wait. A colony simply sits until something touches it.

  • Species-Specific:

    • Tieflings: The demonic origin of zygoms means tieflings make the infestation save at disadvantage — something in their fiendish heritage resonates with Zuggtmoy's influence.

    • Myconids: Will not enter a space containing zygoms. Clearing a zygom infestation from Myconid territory earns genuine gratitude.

    • Undead, Constructs, & Elementals: cannot be infested, but blue milk adheres to them and they become passive carriers, spreading contact infestation to anything they touch.

    • Oozes: Oozes that absorb blue milk become carriers — the milk survives inside them and transfers to the next creature the ooze engulfs.

  • When Harvesting / Any Physical Contact with Zygom: DC 16 Survival or Nature check, proficiency required, gloves mandatory. (DM should secretly tell you if you failed this roll!) On success: one vial of Blue Milk. On failure: Infestation begins.

  • Blue Milk: Extremely adhesive, bonds to flesh and equipment for 1d4+1 days before crumbling. Spores begin infesting immediately on flesh contact. Any creature touching it with bare skin makes a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or is Infested (DM should secretly tell you if you failed this roll!)

  • Infestation: Victim is controlled by the zygom (treat as Dominate Person, no save, no Concentration). Death in 1 weeks x Constitution modifier. Cure: Remove Disease, Greater Restoration, or Wish only.

  • Controlled Host: Attacks and defends normally but guided by fungal self-preservation — protects the colony first. Can speak and appear normal. Does not know it is infested. Behavioral changes become obvious only when the infestation is well advanced.

  • Food: Not Edible.

  • Addiction: None


Gas Spore

Creature and Harvestable Fungus

  • Found In: Underdark — floats in caverns, tunnels, and anywhere corpses accumulate. Found in clusters of 1–6. Also found in Shedaklah (222nd layer of the Abyss, domain of Zuggtmoy).

  • Value — Live: Nothing. It's a hazard. Do not attempt to carry or sell a live gas spore.

  • Value — Harvested Spore Powder: 50–80 gp per vial to poisoners and alchemists.

  • Appearance: Spherical, balloon-like, floating. Possesses a blind central false eye and ten rhizome growths resembling eyestalks. Indistinguishable from a beholder at distance. DC 15 Nature or Intelligence check to identify before engaging.

  • Lore: Gas spores originated from parasitic fungi feeding on dead beholders, absorbing aberrant magic over generations. They now grow from any corpse in the Underdark. Four competing theories on their origin persist: natural evolution from beholder corpses; deliberate creation by beholder mages as guardians; deliberate creation by mind flayers as perimeter defenses alongside brown mold and shriekers; or myconid cultivation as colony sentinels. All four have credible evidence. None is proven.

  • When Harvesting — Spore Powder: Carefully deflate (do not explode) a dead gas spore. DC 17 Survival, Medicine, or Nature check, proficiency required, gloves and face covering mandatory. On success: 1d4 vials of spore powder. On failure: Death Burst triggers at point-blank range.

  • Death Burst: DC 10 Constitution saving throw, each creature in a 20-ft emanation from the gas spore. On a failure: 3d6 poison damage and the Poisoned condition for 1d12 hours. Unless the Poisoned condition is removed, the target dies at the end of that time and sprouts 2d4 Tiny Gas Spore fungi (1 HP each). After 2d6 days these sprouts become Large with 13 HP.

  • Crafting — Spore Powder (Injury Poison): Harvested spore powder applied to a weapon or thrown in a vial (range 20/60 ft). On hit: Death Burst poison effects apply. Worth 50–80 gp per vial.

  • Food: Not Edible.

  • Addiction: None


Cloudspore Mushroom

Environmental Hazard — not edible

  • Found In: Underdark. Also found in Molor, the 528th layer of the Abyss — domain of Juiblex, Demon Lord of Slime and Ooze.

  • Value: Not a trade good. Primarily a hazard.

  • Appearance: Grows in patches. A hazard, not a specimen.

  • Species-Specific:

    • Myconids: Completely immune to the spore cloud. They recognize cloudspore patches on sight.

  • When Harvesting:

    • Natural Alarm System: A patch of cloudspores growing in an otherwise empty tunnel is a natural alarm system — something has been moving through here regularly enough to trigger and re-trigger it. The 24-hour reset means footprints and a recently discharged patch together tell you someone passed through within the last day.

    • Spore Cloud: Cloudspore patches release a spore cloud when disturbed by handling, harvesting, a footstep, thrown object, attacks, or spells. A triggered patch cannot release another cloud for 24 hours. 10-ft radius. All creatures in the area make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or become Blinded and Incapacitated until the end of their next turn. Cloud dissipates after 1 round.

    • Collecting Spores: DC 14 Survival check to harvest without triggering the patch. On success, yields a small pouch of spores. Thrown (range 20 ft) to reproduce the cloud effect once. Single use.

  • Addiction: None


Bibberbang Mushroom

Environmental Hazard — not edible

  • Found In: Underdark . Also cultivated (accidentally) in apothecary basements by people who don't know what they were doing.

  • Value: ~15–25 gp per intact specimen to a very careful poisoner. Too dangerous to transport safely.

  • Appearance: Squat, bulbous, pale. Grows in clusters. Releases visible fumes when a creature lingers nearby. DC 12 Nature to identify before getting too close.

  • Lore: Underdark guides treat bibberbang fields the way surface guides treat quicksand — routes are planned around them, not through them.

  • Species-Specific:

    • Myconids: their fungal biology makes them immune to the fumes entirely.

    • Fey: Fey take double poison damage — they are acutely sensitive to these toxic spores.

    • Fiends: immune to the poison damage but become recklessly Charmed, moving toward the center of the spore cloud.

    • Elementals: Fire elementals within 30 ft of the cluster trigger the chain explosion immediately. All other elementals are immune to the fumes.

    • Plants: Plant creatures take double damage from the fumes — the toxic spores are specifically harmful to organic, living plant matter.

  • Effects:

    • Proximity Trigger: A creature that ends its turn adjacent to a bibberbang triggers a noxious fume release lasting 6 rounds in a 20-ft radius.

    • Noxious Fumes: Creatures in the cloud take 1d4 poison damage per turn. DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take an additional 2d4 poison damage (half on success).

    • Fire Trigger: Any open flame within 30 ft. of a bibberbang causes a chain explosion through the entire cluster. All creatures in the area take fire damage.

    • Destruction: 1 HP. Destroyed by almost anything.

    • Resistances: Immune to poison and psychic damage.

  • Harvesting / Crafting — Bottled Fumes: Harvest as an Action, empty vial + DC 17 Survival or Nature check, proficiency required, no flame within 30 ft. On success: one sealed vial of compressed bibberbang spores. Thrown as a flask (range 20/60 ft) — releases a 10-ft radius noxious cloud for 3 rounds on impact. DC 13 Constitution saving throw or 2d4 poison damage (half on success) per turn. Failure on the harvest check triggers the Noxious Fumes.

  • Food: Not Edible.

  • Addiction: None


Barrelstalk

  • Found In: Underdark

  • Value: 5 gp

  • Food: not edible

  • Effects: They grow up to 8 feet in height and 5 feet in diameter. A barrelstalk is a large, cask-shaped fungus that can be tapped and drained of the fresh water stored within it. A single barrelstalk contains 1d4 + 4 gallons of water and yields 1d6 + 4 pounds of food (1lb = 1 ration).

  • Addiction: None


Bluecap

  • Found In: Underdark, Material Plane (Surface), Feywild

  • Value: 1–2 gp per mushroom raw

  • Appearance: Tall, slender, white stalks up to 6 inches with pale blue caps. Unremarkable. Easy to overlook.

  • Food: Underdark bluecaps NOT edible raw — faerzress content too potent. Material Plane (Surface) and Feywild bluecaps edible raw, bland, counts as 1 ration.

  • Lore: Called "the grain of the Underdark." Sporebread (also called bluebread) is the most common food eaten below ground — the equivalent of surface wheat bread. Nearly every Underdark settlement has a bluecap farm.

  • Lore: Bluecaps absorb faerzress — the ambient magical radiation of the Underdark — which is what makes raw Underdark bluecaps inedible but their flour nutritious once processed.

  • Lore: Drow use bluecap batter as the base for fried cave insects — their equivalent of street food. Duergar bake it dense and unleavened. Svirfneblin add cave salt and fire lichen paste for flavor. The bread is always bland. The toppings tell you who made it.

  • Species — Humanoids (Drow, Duergar, Svirfneblin): Each race has their own bluecap bread tradition — recognizing another race's version of sporebread is a small but real cultural signal. A svirfneblin who tastes duergar-style dense unleavened bluebread knows immediately who made it and roughly where they came from.

  • Species — Myconids: Consider bluecap cultivation by other races perfectly acceptable — it is fully domesticated fungus and therefore not kin. No objection to its harvest. A useful diplomatic gift showing cultural awareness without sacrificing anything precious.

  • Species — Fey: Surface and Feywild bluecaps carry a faint sweetness compared to their Underdark counterparts. A fey offered Feywild sporebread — especially with honey or foraged fruit added — finds it genuinely pleasant. A small but reliable goodwill gesture.

  • Crafting — Food — Sporebread: Ground bluecap spores (any mortar, no proficiency needed) = bluecap flour. Baked into bread with water and heat: one loaf = 3 rations. Bland but nutritious. Any creature can do this with minimal effort.

  • Crafting — Anti-Poison Stew: Bluecap caps (not spores) + water, Herbalist or Alchemist's Supplies and proficiency (1 hr during a Rest, no roll required) = a broth that neutralizes one active poison effect in the drinker. Functions as non-magical lesser restoration for poison only.

  • Crafting — Bluecap Ale: Bluecap flour + water, Brewer's Supplies and proficiency (2 hrs during a Rest, no roll required) = a weak, bland ale. Counts as 2 rations per flask. Duergar drink it when they can't get nimergan. Nobody drinks it by choice.

  • Addiction: None


Ripplebark Mushroom.

  • Found In: Underdark

  • Value: 1–2 sp per pound as food. Worth more already cooked and seasoned.

  • Appearance: Shelf-like formations resembling masses of rotting flesh. Brown, fuzzy-textured.

  • Food: Edible raw. Roasted is significantly better. One large shelf yields 1d4+6 pounds of food. 1lb = 1 ration.

  • Crafting — Hearty Underdark Stew: Ripplebark + any other mushroom + any meat or fat, Cook's Tools and proficiency (1 hr during a Rest, no roll needed) = a genuinely good meal that counts as a short rest's worth of Hit Dice recovery and removes one level of Exhaustion.

  • Species — Orcs and Half-Orcs: Orcs eat ripplebark regularly — it's a staple in orc camps near Underdark entrances and mountain caves. An orc NPC offered ripplebark reacts like it's comfort food.

  • Species — Dwarves: Dwarves call it "arantym" and use it as emergency rations.

  • Species — Drow: Consider ripplebark peasant food.

  • Addiction: None


Trillimac Mushroom.

  • Found In: Underdark.

  • Value: ~4 gp per foot of stalk as food (a 4-ft stalk = ~16 gp in food value). Cap material worth 2–5 gp per sheet to cartographers, scribes, and hatmakers.

  • Appearance: 4–5 ft tall cultivated, 3 ft wild. Light gray stalk, broad flat gray-green cap 14–33 inches across. Leathery cap surface.

  • Lore: Trillimac caps are the primary writing material of the Underdark — the equivalent of surface parchment. Maps, contracts, spell scrolls, and records scratched on trillimac are common throughout Underdark settlements. A document on trillimac is definitively from the Underdark.

  • Food — Stalk: Cleaned, soaked in water 1 hour, dried by fire = bread-like food. 1d6+4 pounds per stalk. 1 lb = 1 ration.

  • Material — Cap: Cut and cleaned cap = leathery writing surface. Takes dyes and inks well. Functions as parchment, scroll material, or map material. One cap yields 2–4 usable sheets depending on size. Lasts years if kept dry.

  • Crafting — Scroll Blank: Cleaned trillimac cap sheet + any ink, no proficiency required (1 hr during a Rest, no roll required) = a functional scroll blank. Scribing spells onto trillimac follows normal scroll crafting rules but costs nothing for the paper/parchment component.

  • Crafting — Underdark Map: Trillimac sheet + ormu ink or any pigment, Cartographer's Tools and proficiency (1 hr during a Rest, no roll needed) = a durable map that survives moisture, heat, and rough handling better than paper.

  • Crafting — Trillimac Hat: A fresh, large cap shaped while damp and dried to form (no tools, DC 10 Dexterity, 1 hr during a Rest) = a functional wide-brimmed hat.

  • Addiction: None


Waterorb Mushroom.

  • Found In: Underdark.

  • Value: 3–5 sp per orb in areas where fresh water is scarce.

  • Appearance: Bulbous, round, pale. Sits in shallow water looking vaguely like a smooth stone or large egg.

  • Food & Water: Squeeze like a sponge = 1 gallon of clean, drinkable water + 1 lb of chewy, tasteless food (counts as 1 ration).

  • Effect — Water Dowsing: A character holding a waterorb near tunnel walls can feel it faintly swell toward moisture sources within 30 ft (DC 12 Perception to notice). Not magical — just the fungus reacting to humidity. Useful for finding hidden underground streams or water-filled passages behind rock.

  • Addiction: None


Zurkhwood Mushroom

  • Found In: Underdark. Widely cultivated by nearly every Underdark race.

  • Value — Lumber: 5–15 gp per cut plank depending on quality and grain pattern.

  • Value — Spores (food): 1–2 sp per pound of food.

  • Appearance: 30–40 ft tall. Tree-like in silhouette. Hard, woody stalks with distinctive internal grain patterns revealed by cutting.

  • Lore: Zurkhwood is the oak of the Underdark. Every surface material made from wood has an Underdark equivalent made from zurkhwood — furniture, barrels, doors, wagon beds, weapon hafts, bowls, coffins, bridges, and boats.

  • Food : grain-like, yields 1d4+4 pounds of food per specimen. Ground up, baked into rough bread, or eaten raw. Bland but nutritious.

  • Material — Lumber: Functions identically to hardwood for any crafting purpose. HP and AC of zurkhwood objects = treated as hardwood (AC 5, 10 HP per inch of thickness). Floats in water.

  • Crafting — Zurkhwood Raft: 3 cut zurkhwood stalks + rope or vine binding, Carpenter's Tools and proficiency (DC12 roll only needed if no proficiency) = a functional raft carrying up to 4 Medium creatures and gear. Takes 4 hours to build. Floats indefinitely. Essential for Darklake travel.

  • Addiction: None


Nightlight Mushroom.

  • Found In: Underdark only. Used as a temporary light source by travelers. Grows in natural clusters.

  • Value: 5–10 gp per frond to alchemists. The living plant itself is worth more intact than harvested.

  • Appearance: Tall, tube-shaped, bioluminescent. Grows 1d6+4 feet tall.

  • Effect — Touch Behavior: Touch-sensitive — contact from any creature or object extinguishes the light until touched again. Uprooted or destroyed: goes dark after 1 round. Resistant to piercing; immune to fire, poison, necrotic, radiant, and psychic damage.

  • Lore: Entire districts of Underdark settlements are lit by cultivated nightlight clusters — they are infrastructure as much as flora. A tunnel lined with them means someone maintains this route.

  • Lore: Their touch-sensitivity makes them a natural alarm system — a cluster that's already dark in a "safe" area means something recently passed through.

  • Effect — Light Source: Bright light 15 ft, dim light 15 ft beyond that. Goes dark on touch; touch again to relight. Uprooted, lasts 1 round then dark permanently.

  • When Harvesting: DC 12 Nature check when interacting carefully = yields one Nightlight Frond (alchemical ingredient) without destroying the stalk. Failure still extinguishes the light.

  • Crafting — Hearthlight Bomb: 3 Nightlight Fronds → Essence of Nightlight + oil or alcohol, Herbalist or Alchemist's Supplies and proficiency, no roll required = Hearthlight Bomb. Thrown up to 60 ft, bursts on impact — creates a Dancing Lights effect in a 30-ft radius for 10 rounds (1 minute). Worth ~13 gp.

  • Species — Undead: Mindless undead are drawn toward bright light sources if they have no other stimulus — a planted nightlight can be used to lure and redirect them away from a campsite.

  • Addiction: None


Nilhogg's Nose Mushroom.

  • Found In: Underdark

  • Value: 10–20 gp, especially to scouts, hunters, and rangers

  • Appearance: Small, unremarkable.

  • Lore: Named either for the gnomish explorer Nilhogg who first catalogued it, or — more colorfully — because eating one makes your nose run profusely for the duration.

  • Species:

    • Beast — Underdark-dwelling beasts such as cave fishers or rothe that consume it become agitated and hyperaware of scent trails, sometimes pursuing smells obsessively for the duration.

    • Fey — Some fey reportedly enjoy the sensation and seek it out willingly.

    • Dragon — A dragon's already overwhelming sense of smell is pushed into painful overstimulation.

  • Consumed:

    • Effect: Action or Bonus action, you eat the mushroom. You gain advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks based on smell for 1d4 hours.

    • Downside: For the same duration, you have disadvantage on saving throws against any effect based on smell. Your nose also runs profusely for the entire duration.

  • Addiction: Low


Ormu Mushroom.

  • Found In: Underdark

  • Value: Raw powder: 6 sp per jar (paint/pigment grade). 25 gp per jar (scroll/spellbook ink grade).

  • Appearance: Bioluminescent green moss. Powdery surface. Sheds dim light in a 5-ft radius while alive. Faint warm glow visible from around tunnel corners.

  • Species-Specific:

    • Drow: Universally recognize it on sight. Drow women use raw ormu powder as eye shadow — the faint glow makes it a cosmetic status symbol in Underdark society.

    • Other Underdark Humanoids: Duergar and deep gnomes are aware of its value as an ink ingredient but have little interest in its cosmetic use.

  • Effect — Light Source: Living patch sheds dim light in a 5-ft radius.

  • Food: Not edible.

  • Crafting — Phosphorescent Powder: Harvest and dry ormu (no tools needed, no roll required, 24 hrs drying time) to produce 1 use of powder. Can be done over a long rest (counts as 1 hr of the Rest). Applied to surfaces, glows faintly for 1 week before fading.

  • Crafting — Glowing Paint: Ormu powder + glowworm juice, no proficiency required, 1 hr during a Rest, no roll required = 1 jar of glowing paint. Visible in darkness, invisible in bright light. 6 sp per jar; covers roughly 10 sq ft or 30 small markings. Lasts 1 month before fading.

  • Crafting — Spellbook/Scroll Ink: Ormu powder + Alchemist's Supplies (proficiency required, no roll), 1hr during a Rest = 1 jar of ink. Spells inscribed with it are visible only in darkness, invisible in bright light. 25 gp per jar. A spellbook written entirely in ormu ink is invisible on a lit desk.

  • Addiction: None


Timmask Mushroom.

  • Found In: Underdark

  • Value: 150 gp per sealed vial of ground powder (enough for 5 uses).

  • Appearance: Squat 2-ft toadstool, beige cap with vivid red and orange stripes. Smells foul.

  • Lore: Tanar'ri demons consider timmask a delicacy — one of very few material-world substances they actively desire to eat.

  • Species-Specific:

    • Demons: Recognize the smell instantly and are drawn to it. A creature holding or offering an intact timmask gets one round of pause before a demon acts aggressively — useful in negotiation or as a distraction.

  • When Harvesting: Uprooting, heavy damage, or destruction triggers a Spore Cloud: 15-ft-radius cloud of poisonous spores. Creatures in the area make a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned. While poisoned this way, the creature is affected as though by a Confusion spell for 1 minute. When the effect ends, the poisoned condition ends with it.

  • Effect — Demon Summoning: An intact timmask offered during a demon summoning ritual grants advantage on the summoning check and increases the likelihood a demon responds without immediate hostility.

  • Crafting — Spore Vial: 1hr during a Rest. DC 17 Nature, Survival, or Medicine check; proficiency required. On success, yields one sealed vial of timmask spores. Thrown (range 20 ft): triggers a Spore Cloud on impact (see When Harvesting).

  • Effect — Necromancy Spell Components: Ground timmask powder used as an additional spell component doubles the duration of Necromancy spells (where applicable) and adds +1 damage per die to damage rolls.

  • Addiction: None


Tongue of Madness Mushroom.

  • Found In: Underdark

  • Value: 9 gp per specimen

  • Appearance: Long, slender mushroom resembling an oversized human tongue. Named for both its shape and what it does to yours.

  • Lore: Named for both its appearance and its effect — a creature that eats one cannot keep a thought to itself.

  • Species-Specific:

    • Drow: Drow use it in interrogation as a confession accelerant — a subject who cannot stop vocalizing their thoughts requires no other persuasion.

  • Crafting — Honesty Wine: Tongue of Madness steeped in wine for 24 hrs + any fruit or sweetener, Cook's Tools and proficiency (no roll needed) = one bottle of wine that functions as Tongue of Madness per glass. Each glass requires a DC 10 Con save instead of DC 12, making it easy to administer casually across multiple servings.

  • Food: Edible. Counts as 1 ration. Tastes unremarkable for something so dramatic in effect.

  • When Consuming: Action or Bonus Action, consume the mushroom. DC 12 Constitution saving throw or compulsively speak every thought aloud for 1 hour. This ends Concentration. Lesser restoration or similar ends the effect early.

  • Addiction: Low


Torchstalk Mushroom.

  • Found In: Underdark

  • Value: 3–8 gp per cap

  • Appearance: 1–2 ft tall. Combustible cap. The bones of previous failed identifications are sometimes nearby, if predators haven't carried them off.

  • Lore: Torchstalks are the Underdark's practical answer to surface torches — they burn for 24 hours, require no oil, and grow wild in the region most travelers actually pass through. Every experienced Underdark guide carries several.

  • Effects:

    • Light Source: Burns for 24 hours once lit. Sheds bright light in a 10-ft radius, dim light for another 10 ft. Treated as a standard torch. Requires Action or Bonus Action to ignite.

    • Explosion Risk: Each time a torchstalk is lit, roll 1d6. On a 1, it explodes. A DC 15 Survival, Nature, or Sleight of Hand check negates the explosion. On explosion: 1d6 fire damage to all creatures within 10 ft, no save.

  • Crafting — Improvised Fire Bomb: 1hr during a Rest. DC 15 Survival or Sleight of Hand to harvest and wrap the cap without igniting it. Thrown as an improvised weapon (range 20/60 ft). Breaks on impact and ignites from friction: 1d6 fire damage to all creatures within 10 ft, no save.

  • Food: Not edible.

  • Addiction: None


Bigwig (Faerzress-Suffused Fungi)

  • Found In: Underdark

  • Value: 50–100 gp each

  • Appearance: 4 inches tall, thin stem, wide purple cap.

  • Food: Counts as 1 ration.

  • When Consuming:

    • Enlarge: DC 12 Constitution saving throw (you may choose to fail). On a failed save, you double in size and weigh 8x as much, functioning as the Enlarge effect from Enlarge/Reduce for 1 hour.

    • Extend: Each additional bigwig consumed extends the duration by 1 hour. Size does not stack — only duration.

    • Tingling Warning: 10 minutes before the effect expires, you feel a tingle, prompting you to eat another or prepare to return to normal size.

    • Cancelled By: Eating a pygmywort, or any magical Reduce effect.

    • While Enlarged: +1d4 damage on melee attacks (as the Enlarge spell), advantage on Strength checks and saving throws, disadvantage on Stealth checks. Cannot fit through standard doorways.

  • Addiction: None


Pygmywort (Faerzress-Suffused Fungi)

  • Found In: Underdark

  • Value: 50–100 gp each

  • Appearance: 1 inch tall, short stem, stubby blue cap with white dots.

  • Food: Edible. Counts as 1 ration.

  • When Consuming: Action or Bonus Action, consume the mushroom.

    • Reduce: DC 12 Constitution saving throw (you may choose to fail). On a failed save, you halve in size and weigh 1/8 as much, functioning as the Reduce effect from Enlarge/Reduce for 1 hour.

    • Extend: Each additional pygmywort consumed extends the duration by 1 hour. Same tingling warning mechanic as bigwig.

    • Cancelled By: Eating a bigwig, or any magical Enlarge effect.

    • While Reduced: +1 AC, advantage on Stealth checks, −1d4 damage on melee attacks (as the Reduce spell). Can fit through any space a Tiny creature could pass through.

  • Addiction: None


Golden Chanterelle Mushroom

Based on Real Life Mushroom and Lore

  • Found In: Feywild, Material Plane (Surface)

  • Value: 5–15 gp

  • Appearance: Bright golden-yellow, funnel-shaped cap with wavy lobed edges. Smells faintly fruity like apricot.

  • Species-Specific:

    • Dwarves: Dwarves are largely insensitive to the tingle — their natural resilience dulls it to nothing.

    • Fey: Fey experience the tingle as music — a faint harmonic hum tied to the electrical source. Some find it beautiful enough to seek out deliberately.

    • Dragons (Lightning): A lightning dragon that eats one experiences a brief, involuntary discharge — 1d4 lightning damage to all creatures within 5 ft. No save.

  • Found In: Material Plane (Surface), Feywild — Savage Frontier, northwest Faerûn; caves along the northern coast between Neverwinter and Luskan; surface forests near oak, beech, and chestnut trees.

  • Value: 50–150 gp per specimen to the right buyer. Extremely valuable to assassins and poisoners. Worthless as food. Illegal in most surface cities.

  • Appearance: Grey stalk and skirt, green cap. Nearly indistinguishable from harmless cave mushrooms. DC 17 Nature or Medicine check to correctly identify.

  • When Consuming — Poison: No immediate effect. After 1d6 hours, make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw. On a failure: take 3d6 poison damage and gain the Poisoned condition. Until ended by Remove Disease, Lesser Resotration, or similar effect, every 24 hrs after, roll additional saves at DC 20 regardless of the first result — on a failure: 5d6 poison damage and one level of Exhaustion as organ damage sets in. On a natural 1 on either save: unconscious and dying.

  • Crafting — Assassination Dish: Requires Cook's Tools and proficiency, no roll required, 1 hr during a Rest. Any creature eating the meal makes a DC 20 Perception (smell/taste) check — on a failure, they eat it happily and notice nothing wrong. Counts as 1 ration. Deathcap cooked into a meal tastes positively delicious. The poison is fully masked by flavor. This is the most dangerous thing about it — there is no warning. Victims feel fine, even satisfied, for hours. Toxins are not destroyed by cooking, boiling, drying, or freezing. No culinary preparation makes it safe.

  • Poison Identification Test: deathcap reacts visibly with silvered water (water stored in a silver vessel) — it turns faintly green. A character with Herbalism Kit or Alchemist's Supplies proficiency who tests food or drink this way as an Action can detect contamination in food or drink before consuming.

  • Addiction: None


Deathsbreath Mushroom

  • Found In: Material Plane (Surface) — cave fringes of the High Forest

  • Value: ~5 gp to goblinoid buyers. Near worthless to most others.

  • Appearance: Large and speckled. Unremarkable — nothing obviously threatening about it.

  • Species-Specific:

    • Goblinoids: Delicious. Counts as a ration. A goblin offered one immediately relaxes — it's comfort food, the smell of home. Goblin shamans use deathsbreath mushrooms in ritual meals — eating them together is a bonding act, a crude communion. Outsiders invited to share such a meal are being offered trust. That the meal makes non-goblinoids sick is considered funny, not hostile. A non-goblinoid who eats one in front of goblinoid NPCs — and visibly suffers through it without complaint — earns genuine respect. Advantage on Charisma checks with that goblinoid group for the rest of the encounter.

  • Effects:

    • Non-Goblinoid Reaction: Any non-goblinoid that eats one makes a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or becomes Poisoned for 5d4 minutes.

    • Social Suspicion: Carrying deathsbreath through civilized surface settlements attracts confusion and suspicion — "why does this person have goblin food?".

  • Food: Counts as 1 ration for goblinoids only.

  • Addiction: None


Dragon Egg Mushroom

  • Found In: Underdark; traded across Material Plane (Surface) as a medicinal commodity

  • Value: 25–40 gp. Sought by healers, smiths, and alchemists.

  • Appearance: Round, egg-shaped cap sprinkled with vivid green dots.

  • Lore: Healers prize them for drawing out toxins. Smiths grind them into a paste to protect skin from burns — a common workshop remedy in dwarven forges. Traded actively in Underdark markets, particularly through Drow merchant companies dealing in herbal medicines and alchemical components.

  • Species-Specific:

    • Undead: The toxin-drawing property works in reverse on undead — applying the poultice to undead causes 1d4 radiant damage as it draws out the necromantic energy animating decomposed flesh. A useful test.

  • Effects:

    • Antitoxin: As an Action, apply a crushed poultice (no tools required). Grants advantage on Constitution saving throws against ongoing poison effects for 1 hour, or substitutes for a Medicine check to treat a Poisoned condition (DC 12).

    • Burn Salve: As an Action, grind into paste and apply to skin. Grants resistance to non-magical fire damage for 4 hours. Does not apply to magical fire or fire-based spells.

  • Crafting — Elixir of Fire Resistance: Dragon Egg Mushroom burned to ash + salt, Herbalism Kit or Alchemist's Supplies and proficiency, no roll required, 2 hrs during a Rest = 1x Elixir of Fire Resistance — grants resistance to fire damage for 1 hour.

  • Food: No nutritional value or effects if eaten

  • Addiction: None


Frosted Mushroom

  • Found In: Underdark — cold caves and frost-touched tunnels. Sold in Neverwinter as a combat tool.

  • Value: 20–35 gp. Priced as a weapon, not food.

  • Appearance: Blue-capped, always covered in a thin visible layer of frost regardless of surrounding temperature. Cold to the touch.

  • Lore: Highly sought after for combat use. Soldiers, mercenaries, and Underdark scouts prize them as cheap throwable weapons requiring no magical training.

  • Species-Specific:

    • Duergar: Duergar foragers collect and sell these to surface buyers at a significant markup, considering them easy money — "surface soldiers pay gold for what we step over."

    • Fey (Winter-Aligned): Winter fey who consume, handle, or get hit by Burst of frosted mushrooms gain 1d4 temporary HP from the cold energy rather than taking damage.

  • When Harvesting:

    • Fragile: Dropping the mushroom (fumble, fall, shove) has a 1-in-6 chance of triggering the Burst: all creatures within 5 feet make DC 13 Con save or take 1d6 cold damage and have their movement speed halved until end of their next turn (frost-burned and slowed).

    • Heat Sensitive: Any fire damage or sustained heat source within 5 ft triggers an early burst. Carrying these near a torch is inadvisable. Burst: all creatures within 5 feet make DC 13 Con save or take 1d6 cold damage and have their movement speed halved until end of their next turn (frost-burned and slowed).

  • Effects:

    • Thrown Weapon: As an Action, throw as an improvised weapon (range 20/60 ft). On hit, the mushroom bursts — target and all creatures within 5 ft make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or take 1d6 cold damage and have their movement speed halved until the end of their next turn.

    • Battlefield Use: As an Action or Bonus Action, crush underfoot to create a 5-ft patch of icy ground (difficult terrain). DC 12 Acrobatics check or fall Prone. Lasts 1 minute or until a heat source melts it.

  • Crafting — Chilling Weapon Coat: Fresh frosted mushroom paste applied to a blade as an Action (no roll required, no proficiency required) = coat one weapon — it deals an extra 1d4 cold damage on the next successful hit only. Coating melts within 10 minutes if unused.

  • Food: Not Edible.

  • Addiction: None


Glowcap Mushroom

  • Found In: Underdark — never grows on the surface. Traded up through Underdark merchant routes.

  • Value: 5–10 gp.

  • Appearance: Bioluminescent. Glows pale blue. Tangy flavor, like diluted lemon. "both lighting the way and dazzling the tongue."

  • Lore: Bioluminescent fungi like glowcaps illuminate entire districts of cities like Menzoberranzan — they are as much infrastructure as food. A patch of glowcaps in a tunnel means someone has been tending this area, or recently abandoned it. Surface merchants who deal in glowcaps are almost certainly connected to Underdark trading networks — duergar, svirfneblin, or drow intermediaries.

  • Species-Specific:

    • Drow: Glowcaps are so common in drow cities they're considered peasant food. A drow offered one as a special treat finds the gesture either pathetic or deeply insulting depending on their mood.

  • Effects:

    • Light Source: A single glowcap sheds dim light in a 5-ft radius. A cluster of 6+ sheds bright light in a 10-ft radius and dim light for another 10 ft. Goes dark permanently if killed or destroyed.

    • Glow Marker: As an Action, crush and smear glowcap juice on a surface. Glows for 24 hours before fading. Used to mark routes, leave messages, or tag locations invisibly in daylight.

    • Spoilage: Spoils quickly if exposed to bright or dry environments.

    • Non-Stealthy: Carrying glowcaps in the dark makes the carrier visible — disadvantage on Stealth checks.

  • Crafting — Duergar Stew: Glowcap + another mushroom + salt + any meat or fat, Cook's Tools and proficiency, no roll required, 1 hr during a Rest = a hearty stew that counts as a Short Rest's worth of Hit Dice recovery without stopping travel. The glow fades when cooked but the flavor intensifies.

  • Food: Delicious and edible. Counts as 1 ration. Spoils quickly if exposed to bright or dry environments. It's a key ingredient in duergar fragrant fungus stew — a dish with a bright, sharp flavor. Genuinely tasty — one of the few Underdark foods surface-dwellers actually enjoy.

  • Addiction: None


Greensleep Mushroom

  • Found In: Material Plane (Surface) — Moonsea region, near the city of Phlan

  • Value: 15–30 gp to poisoners, spies, and infiltrators. Essentially worthless as food.

  • Appearance: Green-capped. Unremarkable looking. DC 14 Nature or Medicine to identify correctly.

  • Effects — Delayed Sleep: Ground to powder, dissolves completely in water, wine, or soup. DC 16 Perception (taste/smell) to detect. When Consumed: Lethargy sets in roughly 2 hours after consumption with no immediate warning. After 2 hours: DC 13 Constitution saving throw or fall Unconscious for 1d4 hours. On a success: Poisoned and Incapacitated for 30 minutes instead.

  • Crafting — Potion of Sleep: Ground greensleep + flower petals + clean water, Herbalism Kit and proficiency (DC 14 roll required or else botched) = a Potion of Sleep (use Oil of Taggit stats https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/144-oil-of-taggit-contact).

  • Food: No nutritional value or effect if eaten in other ways

  • Addiction: Low — the drowsy euphoria before sleep onset is pleasant enough that some seek it recreationally and find they cannot sleep without it.


Rogue's Morsel Mushroom

  • Found In: Material Plane (Surface), Underdark

  • Value: 5 gp per specimen

  • Appearance: Small, grey. Grows low, hidden in tree shadow.

  • Lore: The name is earned — these are the mushrooms rogues, bandits, and fugitives eat when laying low with nothing else. Finding a cache recently stripped from a tree cluster means someone has been hiding here. Frequently referenced in tales of roguish survival — the mushroom you eat when you can't risk a fire or a market.

  • Species-Specific:

    • Halflings: Gain advantage on their next Stealth check after eating one while Hidden.

    • Gnomes: Deep gnomes who eat one while underground gain Tremorsense 10 ft for 1 hour

    • Beasts: Forest beasts that consume one become calm and non-threatening for 1 hour.

    • Tieflings: Become acutely paranoid for 30 minutes — advantage on Insight checks but Frightened of any creature that moves toward them unexpectedly.

    • Elves: Cannot be Surprised for 1 hour after eating one while resting in the wild.

    • Aberrations: when consuming, Stunned for 1 round — briefly disrupts senses.

    • Undead (Sentient): Stunned for 1 round — nutrients hitting biological receptors that should no longer exist.

    • Fey: Involuntarily Invisible for 1 round on consumption — the mushroom's camouflage reflex passing through them.

  • Crafting — Potion of Healing: Rogue's Morsel (×3) + any oil or alcohol, Herbalism Kit or Alchemist's Supplies and proficiency, no roll required, 2 hrs during a Rest = one Potion of Healing (2d4+2 HP). smells sweet and faintly herbal.

  • Food: Edible. Counts as 1 ration.

  • Addiction: None


Swarming Toadstool Mushroom

  • Found In: Underdark — parasitic, always found clustered on or around larger mushroom species

  • Value: 20 gp per cluster

  • Appearance: Sickly green and yellowish. A cluster of small mushroom heads sprouting from a single stem of the host mushroom.

  • Species-Specific:

    • Svirfneblin: Svirfneblin who encounter a swarming toadstool cluster gain advantage on Survival checks in that tunnel for 1 hour — the cluster's presence tells them exactly what the local ecosystem is doing.

    • Oozes and Plant creatures: even just briefly touching a swarming toadstool cluster makes them DC 12 Con save or Poisoned for 30 minutes.

  • When Harvesting or Handling — Downside: Handling a cluster bare-handed (no gloves) for more than a minute causes mild skin irritation and a DC 10 Con save or Poisoned for 30 minutes

  • Crafting — Swarming Toadstool Poison: Swarming Toadstool + any oil or alcohol, Herbalism Kit or Alchemist's Supplies and proficiency, no roll required, 2 hrs during a Rest. Yields one dose of poison worth 200 gp. A creature hit by a poisoned weapon makes a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or becomes Paralyzed for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each of their turns to end the effect.

  • Food: Not Edible.

  • Addiction: None


Tessadyle Mushroom

  • Found In: Underdark — grows near regions of high psionic activity, almost exclusively near mind flayer colonies and elder brains. Denser psionic fields produce more abundant growth.

  • Value: 50–100 gp each to arcane researchers, anti-illithid factions, or psionic item crafters. Near worthless to anyone who doesn't know what it is.

  • Appearance: Stringy, fibrous fungus. No cap. Pale, matted strands of wet thread growing from cave walls and floors.

  • Lore: Mind flayers harvest and weave tessadyle into clothing, most notably the Tessadyle Robe — a psionically active garment granting psionic abilities once per day.

  • Species-Specific:

    • Mind Flayers: A mind flayer that detects harvested tessadyle on a creature treats it as theft. No save, no negotiation — immediate hostility.

    • Aberrations: Non-illithid aberrations that touch raw tessadyle : DC 14 Intelligence saving throw or become Stunned for 1 round as the psionic feedback overwhelms their alien cognition.

  • Effects:

    • Psionic Proximity Sensor: Raw tessadyle held in hand vibrates faintly within 120 ft of an active psionic creature. DC 12 Perception to notice.

    • Prolonged Contact: Hours of direct skin contact with raw tessadyle — DC 12 Intelligence saving throw or experience intrusive alien thought fragments for 1d4 hours. Disadvantage on Insight checks for the duration. Non-psionic characters who experience this sometimes seek it out again.

  • Crafting — Tessadyle Cloth: Tessadyle ×5 + Weaver's Tools and proficiency, no roll required, 2 hrs during a Rest = one length of tessadyle cloth — the base material for the Dampening Wrap and Tessadyle Robe. Faintly vibrates when near psionic activity.

  • Crafting — Psionic Dampening Wrap: Tessadyle cloth wrapped around a psionic item or willing/restrained creature, Arcana DC 15, 1 hr during a Rest = Suppresses psionic output for 12 hours.

  • Crafting — Tessadyle Robe (Major Item): Requires 10x tessadyle, a psionic crafter or arcane caster of 9th level or higher, and significant time and resources (DM's discretion). Grants the wearer: Faintly vibrates when near psionic activity, grants advantage on saving throws against being Charmed or Frightened, +1 AC, and one use per day each of: Misty Step, Mending (self only), and the ability to move across difficult terrain without movement penalty.

  • Food: Not Edible.

  • Addiction: High — from Prolonged Contact effect only.


Noblestalk Mushroom

  • Found In: Underdark — often in inaccessible or hazardous locations

  • Value: 175 gp per specimen

  • Appearance: Blends into cave walls — easy to miss without careful searching (DC 13 Perception). Odorless normally. When broken, releases a strongly medicinal aroma immediately distinctive to any herbalist or healer.

  • Species-Specific:

    • Half-Orcs: Half-orcs make the Madness save with disadvantage.

    • Myconids: Myconids that detect a noblestalk's aroma are drawn to it compulsively — DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or they move toward the source and attempt to consume any remaining specimens.

    • Oozes: Oozes that absorb a noblestalk are healed to maximum HP but immediately split if at or above half their maximum — the restoration triggers uncontrolled reproduction.

  • When Harvesting: Destroyed instantly by fire. Also destroyed if dropped, thrown, or handled carelessly.

  • Effects:

    • Full Heal: As an Action or Bonus Action, consume the mushroom. Counts as 1 ration. Restore to maximum HP and remove all standard poisons, diseases, and negative conditions (DM's discretion) — functionally identical to Greater Restoration for non-magical conditions.

    • Madness: DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or gain one level of Madness.

  • Food: Edible. Counts as 1 ration.

  • Addiction: High

5-50gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC11 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. A simple, unprocessed root commonly used by goblins. You can chew it over 3 hours, during which you gain Adv on perception checks, initiative checks, and can't be surprised. The juices can stain the teeth and lips with repeated use, leading to addicts being easily distinguishable thanks to their blood-red teeth and lips. Long-term usage can have many lethal or permanent effects. Vicious addiction.


Blackroot (mountain)

Drug (Material Plane mountain)

10-100gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC13 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. This lichen grows on large rocks and boulders found above timberline. When chewed on, it causes the user to have a pleasant, tingling sensation of the lips, tongue, and gums, as well as a sense of mental sharpness and alertness. Adv on all mental saves. If swallowed, it causes nausea and vomiting if the user fails a DC 13 Constitution check. If used for 1d6 hours continuously, the user must make a DC 15 Constitution check — if failed, they experience nausea, but if passed they gain advantage on Perception checks for the next 1d4 hours. Low addiction.


Styxroot (Hell)

Drug (Hell)

2000gp. A root that grows on the margins of the river Styx in the Seven Hells. Eating it raw or making tea out of it makes the individual unable to remember anything that happens to them for the next 8 hours. Con save DC12 lowers it to 6 hours, DC15 to 4 hours, DC18 to 1 hour, or DC20 to completely ignore the effect. High addiction.


Luhix (Abyss)

Drug (Abyss)

2000gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC17 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. Made from the powdered stalks of a plant grown in the Abyss by demon lords to give to brainwashed cultists. Applied to an open wound that is then sealed with either bandages or magic. User has intense pain for the first minute, with -1 to all ability scores. Afterwards, user is immune to pain (they still take damage, but it doesn't bother them) and they have +2 to all ability scores for 10 minutes. Vicious addiction.


Elendran Pipeweed (merfolk)

Drug (anywhere, merfolk)

Weed-like. 20gp for 5 minutes worth of weed. Algae that were considered a pest by the Elendran merfolk, until some crazy surfacer decided to set it on fire and noticed his mind was both sharper and duller at the same time. Gives the user -4 intelligence and +2 wisdom while smoking it, though it takes a minute to kick in and a minute to wear off once the user stops. Low addiction.


Tobacco

Drug (anywhere)

Chewing or pipe. 1cp per gram/use. 2sp per ounce/28 uses. Low addiction


Halfling Leaf / Pipe Weed

Drug (anywhere)

Weed-like. 5cp per gram/use. 1gp per ounce/28 uses. Most often dried, chopped, and smoked. Causes extreme emotions and induces near euphoric mellow-ness and, occasionally, a user will experience mild hallucinations. Side effects include increased appetite and red, puffy eyes. No mechanical effects unless taking a lot, in which case Adv and Disad to relevant rolls. Negligible Addiction.


Devil's Root

Drug (anywhere)

Ayahuasca-like. 5cp per gram/use. 1gp per ounce/28 uses. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC13 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. A black root that is ground up and snorted. The user blacks out and sees visions of hell. Sometimes, these visions allow the user to see into the future. Blackout lasts 1d4 minutes. High addiction.


Fate's Hair

Drug (anywhere)

5-10g per use. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC11 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. A flowering plant with long sinewy fibers much like hair inside the flower. When consumed you feel intense euphoria, and have a type of clairvoyance leading you to the next noteworthy encounter fate has planned for you — ahead of schedule. But, is it accurate or merely a hallucination? Negligible Addiction.


Redroot

Drug (anywhere)

LSD-like. 5-10g per use. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC13 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. The roots of a particular tree found in deep forests, known to have hallucinogenic properties. Make a Wis 13 save; on a success you see all the colors, failed save and you have a bad trip and take 1d6 psychic damage. Additionally, druids can use this drug to go into a trance (out of combat) to enter "the spirit world", gaining somewhat cryptic visions of the past, present and future. Adv Wis checks, Disad Cha checks, 1d6 hours. Low addiction.


Dreamlily

Drug (anywhere)

Morphine-like. 1-10g per use. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC11 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. Essence of dreamlily is an iridescent liquid that draws on the mind of the user and tastes like their favorite beverage. Provides pain relief and feelings of calmness, giving the user 10 temporary HP per use for 1d4 hours. But Disad on things relevant to being numb, like Wis or Dex checks. High addiction.


Sannish

Drug (anywhere)

Morphine-like. 5-15g per use. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC12 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. A bluish liquid distilled from a desert plant. Sannish is known to cause a pleasant state of euphoria, which, along with its relatively cheap price, makes it rather popular. Addicts are easily spotted by the permanent blue stains on their lips. Disad Initiative, Dex, and Wis, take 1d4 psychic damage, but numb to pain for 1d4 hours, plus Adv on Con checks, plus euphoria. High addiction.


Forget Me Nots (bright sunny climate flower)

Drug (anywhere)

5-15g per use. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC11 to resist most effects. These flowers grow in the wild, yellow in color. They can commonly be found in bright sunny climates. When consumed they apply a temporary new life — you believe you have a different life. If a lone wolf Assassin ate one he could very well believe he is a humble lumberjack with a small family in the countryside, at least for a couple of hours (1d4 hours). Negligible Addiction.


Mordayn Vapor / Dream Mist

Drug (anywhere)

Heroin-like. 50-200g per use. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC15 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. Made from the ground leaves of a rare herb found deep in forests, the highly potent mordayn is taken by steeping a small amount in hot water, and then inhaling the vapors from the resultant tea. Raw mordayn powder, mordayn-tainted water, or an overdose can be a deadly poison. Well-known for the beautiful visions it induces and the deadly peril that can come from its sinister embrace. The visions of a dream mist user are incredibly beautiful and poignant. Your normal life seems drab and futile in comparison, and you ache to experience the transcendent beauty of your drug-induced dreams again. Adv on Intelligence checks for 1d4 hours, take 1d6 psychic damage. When the dose wears off, you must succeed at a Wis save (DC 17) or fall under a compulsion to do whatever is necessary to repeat the dream mist dose (treat this as a compulsion similar to that of a suggestion spell). This compulsion lasts for 1d4 hours before fading. High addiction.


Scada

Drug (anywhere)

Opium-like. 10-15g per use. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC11 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. An herb found on certain plains. User gains benefits of a Long Rest, which doesn't count against their daily long rest and can be done in much less time if lucky. User is stuck in a trance-like stupor for 1d8 hours until drug wears off. High addiction.


Druidic Dream

Drug (anywhere)

10-15g per use. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC13 for half duration effects, DC19 to resist most all effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. A mostly benign pill made by druids and sold to whoever wishes to buy some. Its ingredients and manufacture are secrets the druids keep to themselves. When held under the tongue the pill puts the user in a mild state of giddiness similar to being a 'happy drunk' for 1d4 hours, followed by 1d4 hours of sleep with idyllic dreams. Low addiction.


Ghost / Ghostleaf

Drug (anywhere)

Coke/meth-like. 10-20g per use. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC12 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. A small plant found along certain valleys. Gives same effects as the Barbarian rage ability for 2d20 minutes when inhaled, then 1 level Exhaustion and take 1d6 psychic damage afterward. High addiction.


Vodare

Drug (anywhere)

300-1000g per use. Popular among rich businessmen and politicians. An extremely bitter brown powder, vodare is usually mixed with honeyed water or sweet wine to dilute its awful taste. It is made from the crushed petals of the vodare flower, which grows along mountains. It creates a sense of mild euphoria and fierce confidence in those who ingest it. Adv on Cha checks for 1d6 hrs, and take 1d4 psychic damage. Low addiction.


Devilweed

Drug (anywhere)

10-100g. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC13 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. Leaves from the wyssin plant are dried and rolled into a tobacco-like substance and smoked. +2 Str for 1d3 hours. Disad to Wis checks, and take 1d4 psychic damage. User is easily confused and acts skittish, becoming Frightened of any creature that deals it damage. Low addiction.


Redflower Leaves

Drug (anywhere)

20-300g. If used as poison on unwilling creature, creature can automatically resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. These crushed leaves of a tiny red bog flower are known for their ability to improve hand-to-eye coordination. User chooses 1 task related to hand-eye coordination to focus on, lasts 2d10 minutes, Adv to any rolls for that task. Disad to all other rolls, and take 1d4 psychic damage. Medium addiction.


Haunspeir

Drug (anywhere)

50g. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC12 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. Named after a wizard from Neverwinter, haunspeir is sold as a tobacco-like paste or dried and compacted. It is used by wizards and others who need to rapidly boost their Intelligence. Adv to Int checks for 2d10 minutes, but user takes 1d4 psychic damage and has vulnerability to slashing and piercing damage. Low addiction.


Jhuild / "Thrallwine"

Drug (anywhere)

6g. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC15 to resist most effects. This dark reddish brew is made in Thesk from certain grapes, fruits, and herbs grown near the Surmarsh. Slaveholders and overseers use it to strengthen captives engaged in hard labor while dulling their wills and minds. But it's also used for a wide variety of other uses. Disad to Wis checks, +2 Str, user becomes easily Frightened if dealt damage and is extremely susceptible to suggestion checks of any kind. Not addictive.


Sezarad Root

Drug (anywhere)

75gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC12 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. The sezarad plant is a broad, vivid flower with a short, brittle root. When chewed, the root breaks into soft splinters similar to carrot. It increases vitality. User gains 1d8 temporary hit points for 10 minutes, Disad to Wis checks. Low addiction.


Traveler's Dust

Drug (anywhere)

?gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC17 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. Transported and sold in the form of tiny roseate crystals, each a bit bigger than a grain of salt. Dissolved on the user's eye, gives a red-hazed vista of breathtaking clarity. All sorrows sink beyond recall, while all joys are raised like blazing stars. User feels transfigured, alive, and potent, embarking on a journey with their soul or astral form "walking the crimson road." The winding way leads directly into the literal Abyss. If overdosing, the victims' astral forms are transported onto the Crimson Road, compelled to walk toward the gaping pit, screaming and unable to fight the urge. The Abyssal landscape is littered with Demons waiting, hungering for the moment the doomed soul plummets into the pit. Anyone using traveler's dust shows these telltale signs: trembling hands, sometimes slurred speech, and — most telling — eyes the color of blood. If an addict is deprived of dust, the resultant death is an awful thing to behold. Deprived walkers invariably become violent, first toward others, then to themselves. One theory of the dust's origin holds that it is the crystallized blood of a demon. Vicious addiction.


Chaunsel

Drug (anywhere)

10-100gp. When applied upon bare skin, increases tactile sensations and touch sensitivity of that area. Overuse of the drug causes numbness for several days. Often used by thieves or other individuals to work in near-complete darkness. Allows fingertips to feel even the slightest detail or change in whatever they manipulate. Also used recreationally of course. Adv on relevant rolls. Not addictive.


Tansabra

Drug (anywhere)

300-1000gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC15 to resist most effects. A drug that places mammalian creatures in a sort of temporary stasis, formulated from the venom of several specific creatures. To have its intended effect, must be introduced into the user's bloodstream by injection or other means. Induces a systemic shutdown in the body of a mammal, temporarily ceasing all physiological processes along with the need for them to maintain the creature's life. Any internal wounds or bleeding are stopped, as is its need for oxygen. When in the "tansabra sleep" the mammal doesn't naturally heal and can't be affected by curative or healing magic. The duration of this state is different for each individual affected. Any means to reverse its effects, such as rare gem powders and herbs, are a matter of rumor and speculation. Repeated use of tansabra can be lethal. Not addictive.


Babelfish

Drug (anywhere)

75gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC10 to resist most effects by throwing up; not addictive if used this way. Viscous amber liquid with what appears to be a jellied sardine floating in it. It's thick and salty, and as the fish slithers down your throat you hear a deep resounding voice in the back of your head: "Hello." Take 1d4 damage. Your slimy companion is constantly muttering in your ears. The fish inside you translates the next language you hear that you don't understand, allowing you to read and understand but not write or speak the language. The aftertaste is awful and it is so salty that your mouth feels dry afterwards. The constant voice in your head breaks all Concentration; Disad on listening checks. Repeated use may cause madness. Additional withdrawal effect: you have a hard time understanding written language and become illiterate (as a barbarian), but cannot remedy it with skill point investment. Low addiction.


Nip / "Catnip"

Drug (anywhere)

15gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC12 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. Powerful psychotropic drug that causes the user to see the world in vibrant pulsating colors. You experience wild visual hallucinations, with colors shifting and pulsating. The world seems to be much more vibrant, intoxicatingly so; you can't help but stare. Disad to Int, Str, and Cha checks, but become extremely limber — Adv Dex checks. Each turn, you have a 50% chance to act normally; otherwise you take no actions. If more than one dose is taken in an hour, you grow a permanent cat feature. Medium addiction; high addiction for cat-like creatures.


Sutara

Drug (anywhere)

10-100gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC12 to resist effects. Sap of a small plant found on many planes and terrains. When applied to the tongue, the user can speak any language they desire — that is, if they can handle the drug. Incorrect dosage or an unprepared system will result in them speaking in absolute gibberish for the duration. Requires a Medicine (or Nature) check DC15 to get the dosage right. Also take 1d6 psychic damage. Lasts 4d10 min. Not addictive.


Sharpsugar

Drug (anywhere)

150-500gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC11 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. Smoked from a pipe. Made out of a rare plant that grows only on the Southern Coasts. The gangs that import it are incredibly dangerous. Expensive; indulged in by many performers to give them a boost of energy. Removes one level of exhaustion, gives advantage on perception checks, and adds 5 to your movement speed. User becomes noticeably jittery. Low addiction.


Sleepysalt

Drug (anywhere)

100-500gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC13 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. +5 temporary HP and resistance to bludgeoning damage for 1 hour. At the end of the hour, you fall asleep for another hour; also take 1d6 psychic damage. Low addiction.


Drakeroot

Drug (anywhere)

100gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC11 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. Concentrated nectar of the mandrake plant. When you drink it, you go into a coma for 2 hours. During this coma, your outer layer of skin becomes more like a cocoon. At the end, you emerge with all hit points fully restored and any scars gone. After 24 hours without another dose, you cannot heal using your hit dice or over a long rest without using more Drakeroot. This continues until you break the addiction. Extreme addiction.


Zaegoo

Drug (anywhere)

100-500gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC12 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. Harvested from a breed of gelatinous cube native to the colder regions, it causes a biting cold sensation on the way down — Con save DC12 or take 1d4 psychic damage — then it gives you immunity to cold damage and the ability to withstand cold climates for 3 hours. Low addiction.


Agony

Drug (anywhere)

200gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC14 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. The distilled essence of pain. Mainly used by torturers as a social lubricant, but masochists will sometimes also seek it out. When the thick, reddish-brown liquid is ingested, the user is hit by intense pain, making them unable to move for 2 rounds and having Disad on all ability checks for 1d6 minutes; also take 1d8 psychic damage. During this time, target will likely give up any info. After the pain, user feels intense pleasure for 1d4 hours — although this is less an effect of Agony and more of them appreciating their lack of pain. Extreme addiction.


Brighteye Venom

Drug (anywhere)

500gp, or 1000-2500gp for a Brighteye spider. This venom has, so far, only been consumable by having the Brighteye Spider inject the user. The bite leaves small, purplish holes and blue lines run up the veins. The user's eyes will turn purple and blue, as if the cosmos were trapped within them. Spider bite deals 1d6 piercing damage. A creature injected with Brighteye Venom must pass a DC 16 Constitution save. Failure results in the creature being stunned for 1d4 hours and poisoned for 1d4 days. Passing the save allows the creature to cast the scrying spell, with a spell save DC 20. Low addiction.


Dreamer's Fancy

Drug (anywhere)

1sp per gram/use. 2gp per ounce/28 uses. If used as poison on unwilling creature, user can automatically resist effects. A dark, shimmering liquid extracted from a rare root. When imbibed, renders the drinker unconscious as it plunges their mind into a black void in which they have full control to shape and create whatever they wish. Those who drink from the same root can participate in this lucid dream together, and their creation can be returned to by drinking from this root again. Not addictive.


Reverie Sticks

Drug (anywhere)

50-100gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC10 to resist effects; not addictive if used this way. Thin, hollow sticks similar to those used for incense. When burned, the smoke causes non-hostile creatures to enter a relaxed, dreamlike state. Reverie sticks can also be snapped in half under one's nose; a sharp inhale of its contents delivers a powerful rush of euphoria. The user has Adv on checks to resist fear and Disad on checks to resist being charmed for 1d4 hours, and takes 1d4 psychic damage. Negligible addiction.


Troll Dust

Drug (anywhere)

300-500gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC15 to resist effects; not addictive if used this way. Mixture of various troll parts. When smoked, you gain resistance to acid for 1d6 hrs and it acts as a powerful aphrodisiac. You become distractingly attracted to trolls and things trolls would like. Negligible addiction.


Drektheth Powder / "Dragon Dust"

Drug (anywhere)

300-500gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC12 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. A golden powder with the same consistency of flour, the drug is overly bitter. After consumption, it makes the user feel much stronger than before, although no actual physical change takes place. The drug is also known to cause shifts in personality, usually making the user act boastful and haughty while under its effects. Sometimes this change will carry over into soberness as well for 1d8 hours. Gain Adv to Cha checks relevant to this personality, and take 1d6 psychic damage. Medium addiction.


Devil's Breath

Drug (anywhere)

6000g per use. A tree found rarely in the Sword Coast islands. More a poison than a drug. Upon inhalation, on a failed DC18 Con save, user must follow orders and answer all questions truthfully for 1d4 hours. Not addictive.


Yggdrasil Sap

Drug (anywhere)

10,000gp per use. A legendary, very rare, and powerful drug that lets users see their future, often showing them their own death. However, using it is extremely risky — if the user does not pass a DC 15 Constitution save, they die from the drug's effects. Not addictive.

Pixie's Fire (Feywild)

Drug (Feywild)

Unicorn Wax (Feywild)

Drug (Feywild)

500-1000gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC13 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. Low addiction.


Red Hive (Feywild)

Drug (Feywild)

50-100gp. When smoked you can speak with insects. Other effects include reddened vision, euphoria, a crawling sensation on your skin like bees walking on it, and take 1d6 psychic damage. Negligible addiction.


Faerie Dust / Fairy Dragon Breath (Feywild)

Drug (Feywild)

300-500gp. A very fine, iridescent powder kept in a wax-sealed bottle. It is consumed by unsealing the bottle and very gently wafting the contents towards the nose with a DC 10 Dex check, with failure resulting in an overdose. Take 1d6 damage (elemental type of the dragon). Faerie Dust is actually the collected breath of a faerie dragon — they find it hilarious that mortals can get high off their breath, and will happily provide the breath attack itself with only gentle coaxing. Some faerie dragons make their home in drug dens, exchanging their breath for a luxurious lifestyle and the opportunity to try their pranks upon many citizens of a mortal city. Some particularly daring patrons will pay handsomely for a high "straight from the source," taking the breath attack of the faerie dragon head on and inhaling deeply. Such services are usually only offered with the recipient strapped down on a specially constructed bench. When correctly dosed, instills a gentle euphoria as senses sharpen and surroundings appear more vibrant, providing Adv on Investigation and Perception checks for one minute. When overdosed, the user experiences sensory overload, becoming confused for one minute. Low addiction.


Weirdling Tea (Feywild)

Drug (Feywild)

5sp per gram/use. 10gp per ounce/28 uses. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC10 to resist effects, or Investigation DC13 to realize it's all a hallucination. A tea that shifts in color from orange to blue. When drank, the user sees the effect of a roll on the wild magic table — this is, however, just a hallucination. Not addictive.


Feywillow Fruit (Feywild)

Drug (Feywild)

?gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC11 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. Fruit from a certain tree in the Feywild. The more the user eats, the more they want to eat. It is not harmful in and of itself, just highly addictive. Heavy users are eventually drawn into the Feywild, leaving their friends and families behind, often without saying a word. Extreme addiction.


Lakua (Feywild)

Drug (Feywild)

10-100gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC12 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. Ground silvery bark from a type of tree only found deep in Feywild swamps. Low dosages are generally taken orally. Heavier users often make a paste to apply to their gums. Addicts may smear it into cuts. It gives an adrenaline rush and time seems to slow down, but the duration of the high is short. Death eventually comes from heart failure or self-neglect. +2 Dex, +2 Str for 1d4 min; also take 1d6 psychic damage. High addiction.


Patch (Feywild)

Drug (Feywild)

50-300gp. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC15 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. Ecstasy-like, expanding yourself to feel the sensations all around you. It grants the ability to speak with plants and animals for 1d4 hours. The comedown requires a DC15 Con save — failing adds one point of exhaustion immediately after waking from the first long rest you take, lasting until completing the next long rest. Low addiction, in addition to the comedown.


Cyclops Tear (Feywild)

Drug (Feywild)

5cp per gram/use. 1gp per ounce/28 uses. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC10 to resist effects; not addictive if used this way. A powdered Feywild flower, eaten. Causes your eyes to water profusely. The tears produced taste perfect and are guaranteed to be the best thing you have and ever will taste, though the taste varies by person — and it only tastes that way to the person whose tears they actually are. To everyone else it tastes like tears. Overdose causes one of your eyes to desiccate and fall out. Oddly enough, people with only one eye are immune to this effect, so it is very popular among Cyclops. Negligible addiction.


Sundrop (Feywild)

Drug (Feywild)

5cp per gram/use. 1gp per ounce/28 uses. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC11 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. A bright yellow/orange liquid, naturally incandescent, as if it were a liquefied ray of sunshine. Originally used as a magically synthesized antidepressant, Sundrop tricks the user into believing they are happy, quite literally giving them "warm feelings." Over-usage may leave the user feeling withered between uses, as dependency has rendered them unable to produce dopamine and serotonin naturally. Over time, users commonly begin to build tolerances, requiring greater quantities to maintain the effect. Overdosing causes feverish conditions as the drug radiates through the user's veins, ultimately burning them alive from the inside out. No mechanical effects usually. Medium addiction.


Feydust (Feywild)

Drug (Feywild)

10-100g. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC11 to resist most effects, still roll for addiction as normal but at 1 addiction level lower. A soft white powder that, in the right light, shines with soft blues and reds. The powder tastes like burnt ozone and must be inhaled. Use causes Adv to Int checks but also makes the user seek it out more and more for increasingly trivial tasks; also take 1d4 psychic damage. High addiction.


Slithersoup (Feywild)

Drug (Feywild)

5cp per gram/use. 1gp per ounce/28 uses. If used as poison on unwilling creature, Con DC11 to resist most effects; not addictive if used this way. A liquid that, when consumed in large quantities, makes you feel like your bones are jelly and commonly causes people to writhe on the ground like snakes when taken in higher doses. Negligible addiction, though it often results in addiction since so many saves are required and a fail slips through eventually.

Drug (Underdark)

The Flayed Mind (Underdark)

Disad to all mental saving throws, making this the preferred tool of enslavers everywhere. Grellsvice (Underdark)

Drug (Underdark)
